362952.title: The $K_6$ minor conjecture for triangles and induced $K_{3,3}$ minors
362952.literal_statement:
Let $G$ be a graph. A **minor** of $G$ is obtained by deleting vertices and edges and contracting edges; an **induced minor** is obtained by deleting vertices and edges and contracting connected vertex sets. A **triangle** is a cycle of length three.

**$K_6$ minor conjecture.** If $G$ contains $K_6$ as a minor, then $G$ contains a triangle as a subgraph or $G$ contains $K_{3,3}$ as an induced minor.

This proposes a structural consequence of having a $K_6$ minor, separating the presence of a triangle from the induced-minor obstruction $K_{3,3}$. The source presents it as an open proposal and gives no resolution.
362952.ordinary_assessment: Literal permits edge deletion in induced minors. Under that printed definition K6 minor implies K3,3 minor: use its six branch sets, partition3+3 and delete all unwanted same-side edges. This is a routine literal-definition bridge, not a source-conjecture solution; actual induced-minor definition normally forbids edge deletion and primary body is unread. No intended result claimed.

**Dejter's four-operation conjecture.** Every ETC of $\Gamma$ is obtained via the iterative genus-increasing procedure of Corollary~, departing from $Q_3$, through four constructive operations: periodic extensions, accordion unfoldings, cycle exchanges, and ETCings.

364237.title: Characterization of connected graphs whose geodesic metric satisfies the Menger condition
364237.literal_statement:
Let $G$ be a nonempty connected graph. Write $V(G)$ for its vertex set and $d_G$ for its geodesic distance. Let $\mathfrak{MB}$ denote the class of metric spaces $(X,d)$ such that

$$
d(x,z)=d(x,y)+d(y,z)
$$

whenever $d(x,z)\geqslant\max\{d(x,y),d(y,z)\}$. **The graph characterization conjecture.** The metric space $(V(G),d_G)$ belongs to $\mathfrak{MB}$ if and only if one of the following holds: $G$ is isomorphic to a path; $G$ is isomorphic to the cycle $C_4$; $G$ is isomorphic to a ray $R$; or $G$ is isomorphic to a double ray $DR$. This conjecture reformulates Menger's characterization in graph-theoretic language; the claimed classification connects the four-point metric condition with the global structure of connected graphs.
364237.ordinary_assessment: Complete independent elementary proof and complete source Theorem4.1-to-target translation in ORDINARY-ROUTES.md; source nonempty means at least one edge. Originalv3 and final2025 body target read. Shortness alone is not exclusion.

365117.literal_statement: Let a crystallographic group $G$ act on a lattice, and let a **symmetric short-range-entangled phase** (sym-SRE phase) mean a phase preserving the symmetry and having no intrinsic long-range entanglement. 365353.literal_statement: Let $G$ be an $N$-regular graph on $n$ vertices. For the class of trees, write $\operatorname{crn}(\mathcal{T})=\max_T\{\operatorname{crn}(T)\}$, where $\mathcal{T}$ is the class of finite trees. **Harary and Lauri's conjecture.** The class reconstruction number of the class of trees is 2:

$$
\operatorname{crn}(\mathcal{T})=2.
$$

Harary and Lauri had shown that the class reconstruction number is at most 3; the conjecture asserts that the upper bound can be improved to 2. The supplied text gives no evidence that this conjecture has been resolved.

353991.title: Alspach's decomposition conjecture for abelian Cayley graphs
353991.literal_statement:
Let $G$ be an abelian group with a symmetric generating set $S$. The Cayley graph

$$
\mathop{\mathsf{Cay}}(G;S)
$$

has no loops.

**Alspach's conjecture.** The Cayley graph $\mathop{\mathsf{Cay}}(G;S)$ can be decomposed into hamiltonian cycles, together with a $1$-factor if its valency is odd.

This conjecture extends the known decomposition of Cartesian products of undirected cycles into edge-disjoint hamiltonian cycles. The supplied text states the conjecture but does not indicate that it has been resolved in the stated generality.
353991.ordinary_assessment: Literal omits finite-group standing assumption; infinite connected Cayley graphs have a different Hamiltonicity meaning. No omission-based new result claimed. On finite intended scope quotient Hamilton cycles can lift to multiple cycles; an edge-disjoint simultaneous merger for all generators is missing. Primary unread.
